correctness.rationale: An omitted clique column must contain 0, 1 or m omitted vertices; remaining selected vertices permit at most one omitted neighbor. Domination excludes 111 full-column runs; capacity excludes 101, singleton proximity 1 or 2 to a full column. If b full runs occupy f columns, the exact gap argument gives |S|<=m f+(n-f-2b-2)_+. Optimizing feasible f,b forces the claimed h(n) full columns and no singletons, while the no-full case has at most n omissions, with equality only in three row-oriented exceptions at m=3,n in {3,6}. Cyclic blocks with no 111/101 attain the bound, and the cyclic run-composition formula counts every optimum. Original-graph exhaustive enumeration of ten finite instances plus independent column DP for 192 parameter pairs agreed; infinite proof does not rely on those finite tests.

originality.rationale: The cycle scalar value and the general Cartesian-product upper bound are explicitly credited to their original sources. For n divisible by four the product scalar value is already implied by combining known bounds, not counted as a standalone new theorem. The new statement determines all m>=3, n>=3 product values in the remaining residue classes, classifies all minimum sets, counts their labelled degeneracy and characterizes exceptional full-cycle-row minimizers. Searches of the accessible primary full text, mathematical indexes, and recoverable historical claims did not find a stronger statement or table implying this full result. Historical priority remains provisional, and uninspected sources are not treated as excluded.

value.rationale: The recent 1-limited domination literature studies Cartesian products and open equality questions. This yields a sharp, complete two-parameter clique-cycle family, including an all-minimizer classification and nontrivial four-periodic exact counts, rather than just repeating the known product inequality. The exceptional cycle-row optimizer families at (3,3),(3,6) provide a natural structural boundary. The inference for the previously forced n=0 mod 4 scalar special case is acknowledged as prior implication.
